[Problem]{.card-kicker} **Shifting Sort** [CF 1579B · Shifting Sort](https://codeforces.com/problemset/problem/1579/B){rating="1100"}

One rotation can move any single element to any earlier position while keeping the order of everything it jumps over: rotating $a[i..j]$ left by $j - i$ brings $a_j$ to index $i$ and shifts $a_i, \ldots, a_{j-1}$ one step right. So run selection sort: for each $i$, bring the minimum of $a[i..]$ to $i$ with one rotation. That is at most $n - 1$ operations.

[Solved in full in @sec-part-p5-shiftsort.]{.card-link}

:::
